questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a big city in Europe and that I could go with my friend from back home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, I had no problems with arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any because of covid, but it would definitely have been nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Because of covid there only was an 2 hour online introduction, but it was very unstructured and I did not get anything from it besides extra confusion.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I did not apply for on campus housing as I went to Amsterdam with my friend from back home, who was not a student. So my friend and I stayed at an AirBnB for 5 months, as off campus housing in Amsterdam is a big mess. However, we found a really good place, but it was super expensive. 
I would recommend applying for on campus housing if you have the opportunity. Every exchange student I knew, who applied for on campus housing got it and really liked it, so I did not seem that hard to get.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive, and also, you really need to engage a bit extra in social activities at uni in order to meet new people then.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at VU was easy and I got all the information I needed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could send an e-mail to the institution at any time and they were super fast at replying.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for more courses than you actually need, because some of them might overlap, and then you do not need to apply/register all over but just de-register for those you do not want in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses I took was suuuuper interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There was a lot of presentations and papers during the semester and therefore it got quite busy. Also, the expectations from the teachers and ambitions of the other students were quite high, but I really liked it because it was in a good and motivating way.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The students had more responsibility and in general more work to do, but they also participated more.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: We did not have to buy any books as all of the literature was online and provided by the university

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some activities available, but I dod not make use of any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Open mics and festivals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The museums in Amsterdam, they are great! But also, go to the beach!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Denmark and The Netherlands are quite similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to open mics and festivals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dutch people can be a bit more direct compared to Danish people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness towards individual differences.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring a raincoat, an analogue camera and say yes to all the invitations to out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be easier to become friends with other exchange students than the locals, but the locals are also super kind once you get to know them.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned that I cannot plan everything down to the smallest detail as life is unpredictable, but is also leaves room for more surprises.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: People on the masters are often quite settled, so it was a bit hard to become friends with them as they were quite busy and already had a lot of friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
